name: Karnöffel
summary: Oldest European trick-taking card game still played, a four-player partnership game with a chosen trump suit and special high cards.
rules_text: Karnöffel is played with 48 German-suited cards (Aces removed) by four players in two fixed teams sitting opposite. One suit becomes the chosen or trump suit. One card is dealt face up to each player, the lowest face-up rank decides trump; on a tie the earliest dealt decides. Each player then has 5 cards. In plain suits ranking is King, Ober, Unter, Banner, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2. In the chosen suit there are special beaters: Unter (the Karnöffel) is highest, then 6 (Pope), then Ober, 3, 4, 5 (Emperors). The chosen 7 (Devil) is worthless unless led. Left of dealer leads. Players need not follow suit. Highest card of led suit or highest trump wins the trick and leads next. First team to three tricks wins the deal. Table talk and coaching of partner are allowed.
rating_reason: Classic trick-taking, hidden hands, sequential play, fully textable.
